title: Circulating Tumour DNA and KIM-1 in Renal Cell Carcinoma: Why Sensitivity Is Low, What Comes Next, and How to Combine Them
content: Adjuvant pembrolizumab improves disease-free and overall survival in high-risk clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (RCC) after nephrectomy, yet no blood-based biomarker is established to guide adjuvant therapy selection, monitoring intensity, or treatment change. Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) and kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) are the two most studied circulating candidates, with opposite limitations: ctDNA is highly specific yet insensitive in RCC, whereas KIM-1 is readily detectable but lacks a validated decision threshold. This narrative review synthesises published studies, conference abstracts, guidelines, and trial registries available up to 19 November 2026. In the KEYNOTE-564 ctDNA analysis (736 evaluable patients), baseline postoperative ctDNA positivity was only 5.4% (16-variant assay) and 8.2% (64-variant assay); sensitivity for predicting recurrence was 10–15% despite specificity of 96–99%. In IMmotion010, high baseline serum KIM-1 (≥86 pg/mL, not externally validated) was associated with shorter disease-free survival and with benefit from adjuvant atezolizumab (hazard ratio 0.72), whereas the low-KIM-1 subgroup showed no benefit (hazard ratio 1.20). A combined KIM-1 plus ctDNA model achieved a C-index of 0.76 in oligometastatic clear-cell RCC. Neither marker is ready for routine clinical use; prospective validation of locked thresholds and assay platforms, evaluating both as complementary biomarkers, is the most promising path.
